title: deaddrop: generate_drop_id spins forever if 2^24 space exhausted
description: deaddrop.rs:897-911 retry loop never terminates if all 2^24 IDs occupied (fillable via add_drop explicit IDs ~16MB store) - a hang not an error. Fix: bail after bounded attempts with a store-full error.
close_reason: generate_drop_id now performs at most MAX_ID_ATTEMPTS=32 CSPRNG draws (new const with rationale doc) and returns Option<String>; None means the 2^24 space is effectively exhausted or the CSPRNG failed. Callers convert to store-full outcomes: add_drop -> None (doc updated: 'budget or drop-ID space exhausted'), post -> 5.03 ServiceUnavailable storage_full form (PostOutcome::ServiceUnavailable doc updated), matching the existing storage_full vector semantics. Additionally both post() and add_drop() now mint the ID BEFORE evict_for_space, so a doomed (ID-exhausted) request can never evict live drops — the same invariant tnlp established for explicit IDs. True-exhaustion is not practically testable (would need ~16M stored drops); the bound is statically evident and the full suite is green. Verified: cargo test -p lichen-client --lib 130 passed, deaddrop_vectors 24 passed. Commit 4ba8ab3d0d.
